# The shell

The frame an extension's page is drawn in: the app shell and the scroll area inside it.

Read from the source: every name below, its signature, its JSDoc, and — for a type or a class — its own members.

| Name | Kind | Defined in | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`AppShellProps`](#appshellprops) | interface | `Shell.tsx` | What an `AppShell` takes. |
| [`AppShell`](#appshell) | function | `Shell.tsx` | Header, body, footer — with exactly one part allowed to grow. |
| [`ScrollProps`](#scrollprops) | interface | `Shell.tsx` | What a `Scroll` takes. |
| [`Scroll`](#scroll) | function | `Shell.tsx` | The part that scrolls. |

## AppShellProps

```typescript
interface AppShellProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

What an `AppShell` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `header` | field | `ReactNode` | Fixed at the top. A `Toolbar`, usually. |
| `footer` | field | `ReactNode` | Fixed at the bottom. Status, or a form's actions. |

## AppShell

```typescript
function AppShell({ header, footer, children, className, ...rest }: AppShellProps)
```

Header, body, footer — with exactly one part allowed to grow.

The body is a flex column itself, so a `Scroll` placed directly
inside it fills what is left over rather than the whole frame.

**Also** [`AppShellProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-shell#appshellprops).

## ScrollProps

```typescript
interface ScrollProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

What a `Scroll` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axis` | field | `"y" | "x"` | Scroll sideways instead. A wide table, not a long list. |

## Scroll

```typescript
function Scroll({ axis = "y", className, ...rest }: ScrollProps)
```

The part that scrolls.

`overscroll-behavior: contain`, so reaching the end does not chain
the scroll to the host page behind the frame — an extension that
scrolls igni when its own list bottoms out feels like a bug in
igni.

Not focusable by default. A scrollable region that holds no
focusable children is unreachable by keyboard, so pass
`tabIndex={0}` when that is the case; doing it unconditionally
would put a stop in the tab order of every list that already has
buttons in it.

**Also** [`ScrollProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-shell#scrollprops).
